reuseNote: First run for this pain; all exemplars researched 2026-10-19. Repair run copied from 20261019-140045.

pew-neighbors.name: Pew Research Center survey on knowing neighbors
pew-neighbors.outcome: 19% knew all neighbors by name, 24% most, 29% some, 28% none
pew-neighbors.limits: 2010 survey; later Pew figures seen only in secondary articles and not checked.
pew-neighbors.locator: "Fewer than half of American adults know most or all of their neighbors."

liking-gap.name: The liking gap in conversations (Boothby and colleagues)
liking-gap.place: Cornell and Yale studies, United States
liking-gap.outcome: Across five studies, people underestimated how much new conversation partners liked them
liking-gap.limits: Mostly students and workshop attendees; not a study of neighbors specifically.
liking-gap.locator: "others like us more than we know"

phila-block-party.name: Philadelphia block party permit
phila-block-party.outcome: Petition signed by 75% of households; apply 21 days ahead; $25 weekend fee
phila-block-party.limits: One city's rules; fees and signature rules vary widely between cities.
phila-block-party.locator: "signed by 75% of the households on the block"

seattle-play-streets.name: Seattle Department of Transportation Play Streets
seattle-play-streets.outcome: Free permit; residents closed streets more than 500 times in 2025
seattle-play-streets.limits: Magazine feature, not an evaluation; non-arterial streets only.

kuow-play-streets.name: Play streets in other U.S. cities (KUOW report)
kuow-play-streets.place: Seattle, WA and at least a dozen U.S. cities
kuow-play-streets.outcome: Similar play street programs in at least a dozen other U.S. cities
kuow-play-streets.limits: 2015 article; the other cities are not named on the page.
kuow-play-streets.locator: "It's free." (on applying to the Play Streets program)

playing-out-bristol.name: Playing Out and Bristol's Temporary Play Street Order
playing-out-bristol.outcome: Two mothers closed their street for play in 2009; 17 Bristol streets applied for the new order in 2012
playing-out-bristol.limits: Parenting magazine summary; Playing Out's own pages blocked access in this run.
playing-out-bristol.locator: applied to the council under a "street party licence"

little-free-library.name: Little Free Library
little-free-library.place: Hudson, WI, now St. Paul, MN
little-free-library.outcome: Todd Bol built the first box in Hudson, Wisconsin, in 2009 as a tribute to his late mother; more than 150,000 registered book exchanges in 115 countries
little-free-library.limits: Boxes cluster in wealthier areas; Whitefish Bay, Wisconsin, required an existing box to be removed under a village ordinance, and other towns shut boxes down too.

buy-nothing.name: Buy Nothing Project
buy-nothing.outcome: Hyper-local gift groups; neighbors hand over items and gifts of time in person
buy-nothing.limits: Membership figures on the page are from an early stage; later totals were not opened.
buy-nothing.locator: "first Buy Nothing group on Bainbridge Island, near Seattle, Washington"

west-philly-tools.name: West Philly Tool Library
west-philly-tools.outcome: More than 100,000 tools loaned to over 4,000 members
west-philly-tools.limits: One city; membership fee not shown on the page opened.

front-porch-forum.name: Front Porch Forum
front-porch-forum.outcome: More than 80,000 of about 260,000 Vermont households take part
front-porch-forum.limits: Figures come from a partner organization; page date not shown.

nyc-event-permits.name: NYC Permitted Event Information open dataset
nyc-event-permits.outcome: Public list of approved event applications, including block parties, for the coming month
nyc-event-permits.limits: License not stated; field names not shown on the catalog page.
nyc-event-permits.locator: "approved event applications that will occur within the next month"

fete-des-voisins.name: Fête des Voisins (Neighbors' Day)
fete-des-voisins.outcome: About 10 million people in France expected in 2025; over 5,000 town halls and housing groups support it
fete-des-voisins.locator: Interview with founder Atanase Périfan on how the fête began

big-lunch.name: The Big Lunch (Eden Project)
big-lunch.outcome: Held across the UK on Sunday, June 18, 2017; organizers estimated 9.3 million people, 14% of the population, at a community event that weekend
big-lunch.limits: Organizer estimate; the 2017 weekend was tied to a national memorial event.
big-lunch.locator: "The Big Lunch took place across the UK on Sunday, June 18"

national-night-out.name: National Night Out
national-night-out.outcome: 400 communities in 1984; 34.2 million people in 10,325 communities by its 21st year
national-night-out.limits: Run with police departments, which not every neighbor welcomes; counts are organizer figures.

seattle-nmf.name: Seattle Neighborhood Matching Fund
seattle-nmf.outcome: $1,077,003 to 24 projects in one 2024 round; small grants up to $5,000
seattle-nmf.limits: One city; groups must match the award with cash, materials or volunteer hours.
seattle-nmf.locator: Small Sparks Fund section, awards up to $5,000

bologna-pacts.name: Bologna regulation on collaboration for urban commons
bologna-pacts.outcome: More than 180 collaboration pacts signed between residents and the city
bologna-pacts.limits: Counts differ by source and date (180 to 800); one city's legal framework.
bologna-pacts.locator: "More than 180 collaboration pacts have been signed in Bologna"

surgeon-general-2023.name: U.S. Surgeon General advisory on loneliness and isolation
surgeon-general-2023.outcome: National strategy whose first pillar is strengthening local social infrastructure
surgeon-general-2023.limits: Summary from a policy institute, not the full advisory; an advisory, not funded law.
surgeon-general-2023.locator: Six pillars list: "Strengthen community social infrastructure"
